articles.title: Baker Mayfield Explains Agreeing to $165M Bucs Contract While Seeing 'Cars' at Theater in New Video
articles.summary: Rather than have Baker Mayfield play out the season on an expiring contract, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers were able to sign their starting quarterback to a three-year, $165 million extension on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Rather than have Baker Mayfield play out the season on an expiring contract, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers were able to sign their starting quarterback to a three-year, $165 million extension on Tuesday.

As it turns out, he agreed to the new deal while at the movies:

NFL head coaching legend has a Minecraft hobby just as impressive

Speaking to reporters about his new deal, Mayfield described it as "life-changing" and praised the Bucs organization for their belief in him leading them now and into the future.

Mayfield, who had previously set the start of training camp as a deadline to get a new deal done, said the Bucs got in contact with his representatives last week and he wasn't aware of anything until Monday evening.

Despite having a lucrative contract in hand, Mayfield explained it doesn't mean he is a made man now because there are many goals still left for him to accomplish, including trying to win a Super Bowl.

Mayfield was set to become a free agent in the offseason, though the Bucs did have the ability to use the franchise tag if they wanted to keep him.

Instead, the Buccaneers were able to get a deal with Mayfield that ties him to the club through the 2029 season. His $55 million average annual salary is tied with five others for the third-highest among all quarterbacks.

This contract is also the culmination of an incredible rebound for Mayfield. He joined the Bucs on a one-year, $4 million deal as a free agent in March 2023.

Mayfield played well enough to earn a three-year deal the following offseason. He proceeded to have arguably the best season of his career in 2024 with 4,500 yards and 41 touchdowns.

While the 2025 season was a statistical step back for Mayfield with 3,693 yards and 26 touchdowns, his 61.3 QBR ranked 13th and was better than Justin Herbert (60.6), Trevor Lawrence (58.3) and Caleb Williams (58.2).

The Bucs have gone 27-24 in 51 starts with Mayfield over the past three seasons. He led them to NFC South titles in each of his first two years, including a playoff victory over the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2023 Wild Card round.

Things are set up for the Buccaneers to be very good once again in a winnable division. Mayfield has proven he can operate the offense at a high level. There was no reason not to get a deal done, and the two sides were able to figure out a few days before kicking off the 2026 season.

Mayfield, with his fresh new contract in hand, will lead the Bucs when they take on the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on Sunday.

articles.title: Cam Heyward Rips 'Stupid' Franchise Tag on Video After Amid Joey Porter Jr., Steelers Contract Talks
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers veteran defensive tackle Cameron Heyward expressed his displeasure with the franchise tag as the team continues to negotiate with cornerback Joey Porter Jr. regarding a new contract.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers veteran defensive tackle Cameron Heyward expressed his displeasure with the franchise tag as the team continues to negotiate with cornerback Joey Porter Jr. regarding a new contract.

"It's stupid," Heyward told reporters Wednesday. "It hampers players. Why should any team be able to take advantage of a player for one year? It's used in negotiations, and I think between the player options, the franchise tags, the way they control rookies, I think it's kind of backwards."

It's worth noting that Heyward is an executive committee member of the NFL Players Association.

As for Porter, he's searching for a new deal as he's entering the final season of his rookie contract .

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Tuesday that the Steelers made an offer to Porter in contract discussions, but it was "not good enough for this one to be deemed close."

Pittsburgh has not been willing to negotiate extensions during the regular season, meaning that time is running out for both sides to reach an agreement.

If Porter doesn't receive a new deal, the Steelers will have the opportunity to tag him in 2027 and prevent him from departing in free agency. Once a player is tagged, they'll have until July 15 to sign a long-term contract with their team or else they'll be required to play on the one-year deal unless they hold out.

"We truly want everybody to just be able to maximize what they can do and their potential," Heyward said Wednesday, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor . "We understand this game isn't for long and every player has to do that. That's just a fact. If you didn't, you'd be a shame on you. You'd be not taking advantage of the opportunity you can, but I wish it would get done earlier. I wish everything was done in February if we could."

Porter is coming off a 2025 campaign in which he racked up 52 tackles to go along with a team-high 14 passes defended.

articles.title: Australians love sport: but can the NFL win them over in debut Melbourne match?
articles.summary: The LA Rams will face the San Francisco 49ers in the first regular season American football game to be played Down Under.
articles.body:
An oval ball, in September, in Melbourne usually means just one thing - the business end of the Australian rules football (AFL) season.

But on Friday, at the unsportingly early time of 7am, 100,000 people will begin filing into the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) for a very un-Australian sporting spectacle - American football.

The LA Rams take on the San Francisco 49ers in their opening National Football League (NFL) fixture, the first time the country has hosted a meaningful, non-exhibition regular season game.

The match sold out months ago, with more than half the crowd expected to be people living outside the state of Victoria. On the official ticket resale site, a restricted view seat is priced at more than A$650 (£350/US$470).

"Walking down the street, it's AFL finals week and you wouldn't even know," says Thomas McMillan, host of the NFL podcast Any Given Sunday Australia.

"It's all NFL everywhere. There are bars that are nothing but 49ers bars or Rams bars. We have a Ram Tram getting around the district. When you're in Melbourne and AFL isn't visible, it shows how big this is at the moment."

Kickoff at 10.35am local time on Friday may not be typical for local fans, but meets the demands of prime time US television schedules and their advertisers.

The league held its first international match in 2007, and over the past two decades the overseas matches have become a long-term strategy to attract supporters and their dollars.

Nine games outside the US are scheduled for the upcoming season, including three in London. But Melbourne is the furthest that players and US-based fans will have to travel.

"Obviously there are question marks when you hear you are playing in Australia," 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey told a press conference this week.

"But it has been so cool… the food's incredible, the coffee's great."

That caffeine reference was perhaps as much to the time zone, as nod to the city's famous café culture.

Melbourne is a mind-warping 17 hours ahead of California where both teams are based, and much of the pre-match attention has been on the two teams and their contrasting approaches to trying to "beat" the jet lag.

For the 49ers, who arrived late last week, their players have had time to get over the long journey, adjust to the time zone, acclimatise and practice at a nearby stadium.

Controversially, the LA Rams are taking things to the other extreme, planning to arrive on Thursday morning local time on a charted Qantas A380 superjumbo, play on Friday, and get back to the US west coast shortly afterwards, in theory to prepare for their next match with minimum disruption to the player's body clocks.

"Definitely it's a gamble," says McMillan. "If they don't quite get things right after the 16-hour flight, you still might have that jet lag, even though you're trying to avoid it."

"And not everyone can sleep on planes," says his co-host Danny Webb. "Whether you're in first class, business class, whatever it is, you're still on a plane."

"And", adds McMillan: "And they're six foot six most of them, so it's going to be even tighter seats".

Despite it technically being a "home" game for the Rams, who bid for NFL marketing rights in Australia under the leagues Global Markets programme, this all means it is the San Francisco 49ers that have more of a presence around Melbourne this week.

And while most practice sessions have been behind closed doors, there have been player appearances at a rally for fans and an AFL match, while ex-stars turned up at that most Australian of traditions, the weekly fundraising "sausage sizzle" at the country's most high-profile hardware chain.

American sports journalist Dontay Atkinson predicts this fan engagement will be reflected inside the stadium and that the MCG will be "heavily red" (the 49ers colour), accusing the Rams of doing "exactly jack squat to sell the NFL brand or connect with Australians".

Writing on X he added: "Fly in, fly out, no contact. I'm sure the Aussies feel great about that snub."

McMillan says he can understand the approach by the Rams, who are seen as contenders for the 2027 Superbowl.

"They're looking at this as a game they need to win," he says.

"We do feel a bit snubbed, and feel the 49ers are doing the right thing

"But it is their job, so that's where the Rams coaching staff has gone 'nah, we're taking this approach'.

"I just worry that they have missed the boat of ingraining themselves as the Australian team. It leaves it open for others, and the 49ers have really jumped on that."

The LA Rams insist there has been no snub, though speaking to the BBC, the club's Head of International Stephanie Cheng dodged the question of whether she would have preferred her players to have been in town this week.

"It's really a culmination of more than four years of work," she said. "It's not just about game week. We have long term rights."

Cheng says the Rams are the only NFL team with a membership programme for Australian fans, and that it has sent coaches into schools and communities to promote "flag football" – the non-contact version of the sport which will feature in the LA 2028 Olympics.

She also points to regular earlier visits by star players including running back Kyren Williams in March. This week its cheerleaders have visited US military bases in Australia before coming to Melbourne, and the franchise has installed a 22-yard floating football field on Melbourne's Yarra River serving as a fan zone.

"From day one, when we've come to Australia, there's been incredible enthusiasm," Cheng said.

While no Australian players will be on the field on Friday, there are dozens playing US college football and a handful in the NFL.

Most are punters, kicking specialists tapped up after showing their prowess playing AFL or rugby league.

But it is the success of Jordan Mailata, an offensive left tackle with the Philadelphia Eagles, who in 2025 became the first Australian to play in, and win, a Superbowl that was a "major turning point in Australia's fandom of the NFL " says Webb.

"Seeing an Australian in what we'd called a skilled position and then winning a Superbowl. It doesn't get better than that".

Friday's game is the first of three matches in Melbourne to be held over four years, under a contract between the NFL and the state of Victoria.

The league's preference, says Gerrit Meier, managing director and head of NFL International, is to have annual games in Australia similar, to the way the game has grown in the UK.

"We're working off the hypothesis that we need to make a commitment to a market," he told Reuters.

And while many US-based supporters are not fans of the international fixtures, these games are here to stay, says Webb, and the hype and the sell-out crowd in Australia augurs well for it to become a long-term fixture

"I had mates four years ago asking why are you doing an NFL podcast? It's not a big sport here," he said.

"And now every single one of those mates are asking me for tickets for the game."

articles.title: Ex-Titans scout, Arkansas State DB Blaise Taylor handed 2 life sentences for using cocaine to murder his pregnant girlfriend
articles.summary: Taylor was found guilty in July of poisoning his then-girlfriend, Jade Benning, on Feb. 25, 2023 by putting cocaine in her lemonade when she was five months...
articles.body:
Former Tennessee Titans scout and Arkansas State defensive back Blaise Taylor was handed two consecutive life sentences Wednesday for the 2023 murder of his pregnant girlfriend and her unborn child.

Taylor was found guilty in July of poisoning his then-girlfriend, Jade Benning on Feb. 25, 2023 by putting cocaine in her lemonade when she was five months pregnant. Benning's unborn fetus died two days later. Benning died weeks later of acute cocaine poisoning on March 6, her 25th birthday. The child was believed to have been Taylor's.

Taylor faced trial and pleaded not guilty. Per WSMV in Nashville, Benning's friend, Nijaiha Jackson testified about a phone call she received from Benning on the night that she was poisoned.

"She immediately starts saying, 'What did you do? What did you put in my drink?' Then I heard her say, 'Blaise, you're scaring me,'" Jackson testified. "He said, 'You're scaring me.' And she was like, 'I know you put something in my drink. ... I knew my drink tasted funny. … "You did this so something would happen to the baby.'"

"She immediately starts saying, 'What did you do? What did you put in my drink?' Then I heard her say, 'Blaise, you're scaring me,'" Jackson testified. "He said, 'You're scaring me.' And she was like, 'I know you put something in my drink. ... I knew my drink tasted funny. …

"You did this so something would happen to the baby.'"

A Nashville jury convicted him on four counts on July 1: One count of first-degree felony murder of Benning, one count of second-degree murder of Benning, one count of first-degree murder of an unborn child and one count of first-degree felony murder of the unborn child. Per WSMV, the jury took two hours to deliberate before reaching its verdicts.

Taylor faced his sentencing hearing on Wednesday, and the jury recommended two consecutive life sentences and an additional 22 years in prison for Taylor. His attorney, Letitia Quinones-Hollins, issued a statement that Taylor intends to appeal the decision.

"We are extremely disappointed but not surprised by the harsh sentence," Quinones-Hollins' statement reads, per WSMV. "This was a flawed trial of a tenuous case, and we will appeal and look forward to doing so."

Nashville Assistant District Attorney Jan Norman, meanwhile, commented on 87 character witness letters that were offered for Taylor.

"The person described in these character letters, the authors themselves, not one mentioned Jade Benning, not one of them mentioned baby Ivy, and not one single letter out of the 87 letters mentioned anything about what Blaise Taylor did," Norman said, per The Athletic.

Taylor, 30, played four seasons at Arkansas State from 2014-17. He was a team captain and earned All-Sun Belt honors. After college, Taylor worked as a scout for the Titans through 2023. He later worked for Utah State as a defensive analyst.

articles.title: The Ringer somehow has the Bengals QB room ranked 10th in the NFL
articles.summary: Joe Burrow and Joe Flacco were behind the Bears, among other teams.
articles.body:
Joe Burrow is arguably the most talented QB in the league.

Joe Flacco is a former Super Bowl MVP who still has a lot of life left in his arm.

Yet somehow, The Ringer 's Diante Lee thinks those two are only the 10th-best QB room in the NFL, behind even that of the Chicago Bears .

Burrow is an established postseason force, but he hasn't ever seriously factored into the MVP or All-Pro conversation. And after three consecutive seasons of missing the playoffs (including two in which Burrow suffered injuries), it's fair to wonder whether he'll deliver a return on his current $275 million deal. Cincinnati's backup plan is confusing. The Bengals have wisely put veteran pocket passers behind Burrow, himself a pocket passer, for the sake of scheme continuity, but the 41-year-old Flacco no longer provides much upside. He was a sack and turnover machine at times last season. And Cincinnati's third quarterback, 40-year-old Josh Johnson , puts the "journey" in journeyman. Flacco's $6 million salary is a huge overpay relative to his performance on the field, and the $1.5 million for Johnson's veteran minimum deal could've been spent on a younger, more interesting developmental option that the Bengals could keep behind Burrow long term.

articles.title: Browns news: Deshaun Watson speaks up on proving his NFL clock hasn't run out
articles.summary: After being named the Cleveland Browns’ starting quarterback for Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, all eyes are on Deshaun Watson to see if he can ret...
articles.body:
After being named the Cleveland Browns ' starting quarterback for Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars , all eyes are on Deshaun Watson to see if he can return to his vintage form, or if he will be exiled to the bench for good in favor of a deep QB room headlined by Shedeur Sanders .

While the general mood around watching Watson start at quarterback in 2026 isn't exactly high, the former Houston Texans star doesn't think fans should write him off just yet, as he still believes he can be a high-quality starter at the NFL level.

"I can't focus on the future. I got to focus on now. You know, if I try to look ahead and I get distracted on not focusing on what I need to do now, then, you know, who knows what the future might hold," Watson said.

articles.title: Former Washington football star WR dealing with foot injury
articles.summary: Former Washington Huskies star wide receiver Rome Odunze popped up on the injury report with a foot issue ahead of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
After Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze was forced to miss five games in 2025 with a stress fracture in his foot, the former Washington Huskies superstar and No. 9 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft has popped up on the injury report again ahead of the team's season opener against the Carolina Panthers .

While he's dealing with another foot injury, head coach Ben Johnson stated that it's not related to the issue that sidelined the 2023 Consensus All-American.

"I don't believe he'll be out there today, but we're hopeful he'll be out there on Sunday," Johnson said during a press conference on Tuesday, adding that Odunze is day-to-day. He was listed on Wednesday's injury report as a limited participant in practice, which is an estimation, as the Bears didn't go through a workout.

The issue first popped up in practice on Thursday, September 3, when Odunze was forced to leave practice early with the injury.

As Johnson looks ahead to his second season, Odunze is expected to be a key piece of his offense after establishing strong chemistry with quarterback Caleb Williams across their first two seasons in the NFL together, and to lead a group of promising young pass catchers that also includes wide receiver Luther Burden and tight end Colston Loveland .

Across his first two years in the league, Odunze has played in 20 games and compiled 98 catches for 1,395 yards and 9 touchdowns.

articles.summary: NBC's pregame show spotlighted the Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini scandal before the New England Patriots' season opener against the Seattle Seahawks.
articles.body: Mike Vrabel and the New England Patriots want everyone to forget that the coach and the franchise by extension were tied to an embarrassing scandal when the Dianna Russini story surfaced in April. But here we are on the night the NFL season kicks off and, nope, nobody has forgotten. NBC, bless their hearts, didn't forget. THE ATHLETIC PROBES DIANNA RUSSINI AND MIKE VRABEL RELATIONSHIP WHILE CONSIDERING GETTING IN BED WITH THE NFL On their pregame show prior to the Patriots season-opening game against the Seattle Seahawks, the relationship between Vrabel and Russini was highlighted. And discussed. MIKE VRABEL STEPPING AWAY FROM PATRIOTS INDEFINITELY TO SEEK COUNSELING AMID DIANNA RUSSINI CONTROVERSY "Remember in the offseason, Vrabel missed the final day of the draft in April to seek counseling after photos were published of him and longtime NFL reporter Dianna Russini," host Maria Taylor told the audience before moving on to the acquisition of A.J. Brown and asking if the team is better on paper now. This is not what the Patriots want. It's definitely not what Vrabel wants because he has mostly declined to answer questions on the topic since training camp opened with one exception when he was asked about that family counseling. MIKE VRABEL, ONE MONTH AFTER STARTING 'COUNSELING,' TELLS REPORTERS HE LOVES HIS WIFE Vrabel deflected from the topic that time. DIANNA RUSSINI'S RELATIONSHIP WITH MIKE VRABEL IN CLEAR VIOLATION OF STANDARDS, THE ATHLETIC'S REVIEW SAYS He also declined to address the issue last week when The Athletic published its standards review which found the reporter's relationship with Vrabel was "in clear violation" of the media company's standards. "This team has fully moved past all the offseason stuff," analyst Devin McCourty, a former Patriots safety, said on air. "The Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini stuff, they're not talking about it. "You won't hear a player mention anything. They're focused solely on this season." The Patriots may indeed be fully focused on the start of the regular season. But they do not write the script for the media which may continue to mention the offseason scandal early this season as a way of recapping all that happened to the team and its coach. And, obviously, if the season in any way goes against expectations and the Patriots struggle, it won't be a reach for reporters to ask if the scandal that dominated national headlines from April to June distracted from any preparation. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS One more thing: Russini, who resigned from The Athletic following the publishing of her photos with Vrabel, has reportedly vowed to address the issue once she returns to public life. Depending on what narrative that address follows, the Patriots may once again find themselves trying to manage a public relations issue. (Just a guess here: Russini will find no fault with anything she did during her many-years-old relationship with Vrabel dating back to when he coached the Tennessee Titans). articles.title: Commanders' Jayden Daniels is ready to quiet the critics entering his third NFL season
articles.summary: As magical as Jayden Daniels’ rookie year was, the quarterback's sophomore season was equally underwhelming.  Now the pressure is high on Daniels and the Com...
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. (AP) — As magical as Jayden Daniels ' rookie year was, the quarterback's sophomore season was equally underwhelming. He played in just seven games for the Washington Commanders , who stumbled to a 5-12 record.

Now the pressure is high on Daniels and the Commanders entering the 2026 season. His durability has been questioned. The offensive line in front of him has been average at best during training camp, especially after left tackle Laremy Tunsil injured his left triceps .

Daniels and Washington's starting offense did little to quiet those concerns in recent weeks. The starters played just three snaps in the preseason — one drive at Detroit — and Daniels was pressured or sacked on both of his drop-backs. The offensive line struggled significantly the following week during a joint practice with Baltimore .

Daniels said Wednesday he's not concerned about the outside scrutiny.

"Everybody has an opinion, no matter if it's good or bad," he said. "It's nothing I could really control to the point everybody's going to say something. The only thing that matters to me is the people inside that building, my family and helping the Washington Commanders win football games to be the best version of myself."

Offensively, the Commanders should look a lot different this season than they did the past two years under Kliff Kingsbury. New offensive coordinator David Blough prefers his QB to spend more time under center, something Daniels has never done before to this extent.

Learning a new system led to more training camp snaps for Daniels. That was a source of excitement for coach Dan Quinn.

"Just knowing how much work that he's put into the system, I'd like to see that execution take place," Quinn said. "He's really in very good command of it. … The way he's able to express himself in the offense, I can't wait to see that."

The Commanders didn't showcase much of what the new offense will look like when facing Miami and Baltimore during joint practices. That was by design, with road divisional matchups at Philadelphia and Dallas to begin the season.

"I guess we all got to see on Sunday," Daniels said when asked about the offense's capabilities. "We'll see Week 1 and then next week, and hopefully we look up Week 15 and we're a better offense than we were Week 1."

Daniels goes into his third season with four-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Stefon Diggs and tight end Chig Okonkwo added to a group of skill players led by top receiver Terry McLaurin . Daniels and Diggs have already started to form solid chemistry.

"He's a superstar," Diggs said of Daniels. "He can put the ball anywhere. He can use his legs. He makes good decisions. As a receiver, you just want to be open."

Through his first two seasons, much of the Commanders' offensive success relied on Daniels' heroics. The goal now is for that not to be the case.

"I trust those guys to go out there and make plays," Daniels said. "I love basketball. Just being a point guard, getting the ball to playmakers, the ball in space, and let them do their thing. When it's time for me ... to go get a bucket, I've got to go do that sometimes."

articles.title: 'A new narrative.' Why the Bengals are confident in their linebackers
articles.summary: By now, you've probably heard some version of the preseason patter around the Cincinnati Bengals defense.
articles.body:
See the food coming to Paycor Stadium for Bengals season

Eventually, all the platitudes and happy that color the NFL's preseason give way to reality and hard truths. That's where the Cincinnati Bengals are with their linebackers.

By now, you've probably heard some version of the preseason patter around the Bengals defense − that it's improved, that there are waves of rushers, it has more talent, more depth and players better-suited for leadership roles compared to the defense of a year ago.

To Cincinnati's credit, the front office spared little expense during the offseason in order to upgrade its defensive personnel. The publicly available sample size is small, and the defense might still have some holes based on the joint practice against the Chicago Bears . Many experts still anticipate these talking points will bear out once the 2026 season kicks off Sept. 13 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

But the one outstanding question looming over the defense is the linebacker position, where the Bengals aren't buoyed by a big-name veteran or a major free-agent upgrade. That makes it an outlier on the roster and a great unknown as two second-year players in Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. are being entrusted with starting roles.

From Director of Player Personnel Duke Tobin to head coach Zac Taylor and defensive coordinator Al Golden, the decision to stand behind Carter and Knight as starters has been explained and rationalized, but that talk can only carry the organization through to the 1 p.m. kickoff Sept. 13 at Paycor Stadium. That's when the season begins and when the truth about the team's linebacking duo will be revealed.

Whether or not they can produce better results than they did during their rookie season in 2025 could dictate how high the ceiling is for a team that speaks openly about chasing a championship.

"Really excited about both of them. They're in the upper echelon of all rep-getters (in training camp), and they needed that," Golden said. "I've said it to you guys multiple times: I think they are playing with confidence. They're able to run it at the line of scrimmage, whether it's stunt adjustments, checks, whatever the case may be. They've done a really good job, and I'm just excited to watch them go play, just go have fun and play with energy and let it loose."

Golden speaks of his confidence in Carter and Knight. Carter and Knight project confidence, too. The two players are drawing on the experience of their baptism-by-fire 2025 campaigns, plus this past offseason and training camp.

In the modern NFL, the preseason doesn't necessarily mean ample opportunities for projected starters, especially in preseason games.

"If you're worried about preseason games, that's not totally fair," Knight said. "If people are watching preseason games — full-speed action is Day 1 of OTAs, Day 1 of training camp. Our offense isn't just running plays for us to make stops. They're scheming us. We're scheming them. We're sharpening iron week after week after week. … I believe it was great work. It felt like game situations, pretty much.

"This whole camp and OTAs has been game-like situations. We're banging left and right. Fights here, left and right. You're not gonna fight if you're not truly getting reps, so I would say camp and OTAs got us ready."

Carter and Knight have also kept the 2025 season in mind, even while that's a painful exercise at times. Carter said he hated to still call upon that experience in explaining his present-day rationale.

The two players ended up as companion pieces in the story of the 2025 Bengals. Their play, and the decision to draft both of them in the 2025 NFL Draft, became a case study for critics as they analyzed the organization's personnel decision-makers.

Carter contended the 2025 season spurred growth in both players by the time they were back at Paycor Stadium in the spring for organized team activities (OTAs). Like the 2025 season itself, the journey through OTAs, periodic offseason downtime and training camp was one they made in lockstep.

It's still just preseason talk, but Carter said he and Knight were confident the team's faith in them would be rewarded.

"We've been through the fire. We've seen the worst of the worst, and we know what the bottom feels like," Carter said. "When you know what the bottom feels like, the only way to go is up. We went to work in the offseason. We made sure that we're gonna write a new narrative. We have ultimate control over it. And we're gonna do what needs to be done. … When you go through adversity, there's nothing that shapes a true man like going through adversity.

articles.title: From NFL opener at Lumen Field: Nick Emmawori is out, other Seahawks inactives
articles.summary: Two safeties missing mean two safeties up from the practice squad for Seattle against New England in the Super Bowl 60 rematch.
articles.body:
Nick Emmanwori couldn't do to the Patriots what he'd done to them in the Super Bowl.

It's tough to terrorize an offense while in a hoodie on the sideline.

The Seahawks ' dynamic, hybrid safety/linebacker was inactive as expected for the Super Bowl champions' NFL kickoff game against New England at packed Lumen Field Wednesday night.

The team listing him officially as questionable on Tuesday seemed like gamesmanship, to keep the Patriots guessing on Emmanwori's status. He hasn't fully participated in a practice since minicamp in June. He has arthroscopic surgery in July on his ankle. He sprained it in February four days before the Super Bowl, then played as part of Seattle 's domination of Drake Maye and New England's offense in Super Bowl 60.

Starting deep safety Ty Okada also wasn't playing Wednesday. He had a hamstring injury.

Their absences forced the Seahawks to sign to the 53-man roster safety AJ Finley. They also elevated from the practice squad veteran safety Rodney Thomas II , a former Indianapolis Colts starter, and running back Velus Jones Jr.

The team waived second-year guard Bryce Cabledue to get Finley onto the active roster.

Finley was back deep at safety with Julian Love in the starting defense during pregame warmups. Love was the only healthy safety on the active roster at the start of the day.

Rookie Julian Neal was outside at cornerback, making Devon Witherspoon free to move inside when coach Mike Macdonald wanted to go with a nickel set with five defensive backs. Neal was Seattle's third-round draft choice this spring. He missed almost all of the preseason and August with a leg injury.

Neal's injury and Nehemiah Pritchett 's struggling in tackling as the third cornerback were why the Seahawks signed former Dallas Cowboys All-Pro cornerback Trevon Diggs late last month. Diggs remained on the practice squad for the opener Wednesday.

NFL rules permit a team to elevate a maximum of two players from the practice squad for each game.

Seattle's other inactive players for the opening game: injured (again) wide receiver Tory Horton , rookie backup guard Beau Stephens, third quarterback Jalen Milroe , tight end Nick Kallerup and defensive end Mike Morris .

The Patriots' notable inactive player was running back TryVeyon Henderson. He was out with an injured ankle.

articles.title: Alleged victim in Antonio Brown attempted murder case forgives him, no longer wants to take part in prosecution
articles.summary: Antonio Brown was arrested and extradited back to the United States after an alleged shooting in Miami in May 2025.
articles.body:
The man who is the alleged victim in former NFL star Antonio Brown's second-degree attempted murder case apparently no longer wants to participate in his prosecution.

Brown was arrested last year and extradited back to the United States from Dubai after an incident outside of an amateur boxing match in Miami in May 2025. The alleged victim in the case, Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu, "has made the deeply personal decision to forgive" Brown, he said through his attorney on Wednesday, via ESPN .

As a result, Nantambu "does not wish to participate" in Brown's prosecution. Brown's attorney is now hopeful that Florida drops the case.

"Forgiveness does not diminish the seriousness of what occurred," Nantambu's attorney said. "It means refusing to allow anger or resentment to dictate how he moves forward."

Brown was detained by Miami police briefly after gunshots were fired outside several hours after a boxing event on May 17. Video on social media showed Brown involved in a fistfight with several people outside of the event. A man who police later identified as Brown was seen pursuing someone with what looked like a pistol in his hand. Shots were heard off camera.

Brown was not initially arrested, and police said they did not find a weapon on the scene when they detained him. But they later issued an arrest warrant for Brown after an investigation.

Nantambu told police on May 21 that one of the bullets fired grazed his neck. He was identified as the man with whom Brown had gotten into a fistfight before the shooting. The warrant stated that Brown chased Nantambu after grabbing the gun off of a security officer and fired two shots at him.

After the incident, Brown flew to Dubai and spent nearly six months in the country before he was extradited back to the United States. He was released on bond and placed on house arrest with a GPS ankle monitor.

Brown later said that he was "jumped" and that he was forced to act in self-defense the night of the shooting. He filed a motion to dismiss the case based on Florida's "stand our ground" law in December.

Brown's attorney, Mark Eiglarsh, said Wednesday that he doesn't expect the state to immediately drop the charges against his client, but he's hopeful that will happen in the near future. If convicted, Brown could face up to 30 years in prison.

"Antonio would like to make his own position equally clear: He forgives Mr. Nantambu," Eiglarsh said. "Antonio wishes Mr. Nantambu and his family peace and holds no hatred or resentment toward him. "From the very beginning, Mr. Brown has maintained his innocence. He did not commit attempted second-degree murder, and he maintains that, under the circumstances presented that day, he had a lawful right to defend himself."

"Antonio would like to make his own position equally clear: He forgives Mr. Nantambu," Eiglarsh said. "Antonio wishes Mr. Nantambu and his family peace and holds no hatred or resentment toward him.

"From the very beginning, Mr. Brown has maintained his innocence. He did not commit attempted second-degree murder, and he maintains that, under the circumstances presented that day, he had a lawful right to defend himself."

Brown spent 12 seasons in the NFL, and was undoubtedly one of the best wide receivers in the league at the peak of his career. He has had several legal issues since his playing career ended. Brown was accused of rape by a former trainer in 2019, though he did not face criminal charges there and that lawsuit was settled out of court. Brown was also ordered in 2022 to pay more than $1 million in damages to a delivery driver that he allegedly assaulted outside of his Florida home. Brown previously pleaded no contest to multiple criminal charges after that incident, and was sentenced to two years probation.

articles.title: Watch Seahawks Raise Super Bowl 60 Banner in Trending Video Before Patriots Rematch
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks commemorated the team's Super Bowl LX victory by raising a banner at Lumen Field ahead of a season-opening rematch with the New England Patriots on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks commemorated the team's Super Bowl LX victory by raising a banner at Lumen Field ahead of a season-opening rematch with the New England Patriots on Wednesday.

Former Seahawks star safety Kam Chancellor led a crowd chant as the banner was unveiled.

Seattle capped off its 2025 campaign with a 29-13 win over New England in the Super Bowl, capturing the franchise's second Lombardi Trophy.

The Seahawks were stellar throughout last year, compiling a 14-3 record in the regular season to win the NFC West while earning the No. 1 seed in the conference heading into the playoffs.

Quarterback Sam Darnold earned a Pro Bowl nod by completing 67.7 percent of his throws for 4,048 yards and 25 touchdowns, while star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba took home Offensive Player of the Year honors after compiling a league-leading 1,793 receiving yards to go along with 10 scores.

Head coach Mike Macdonald's defense was also dominant, ranking No. 1 in the NFL by allowing a mere 17.2 points on a weekly basis. Seattle ranked No. 5 among all teams with 25 total takeaways as well.

The Seahawks continued to excel during their playoff run, outscoring their three opponents 101-46.

Seattle held New England scoreless through the first three quarters of their Super Bowl matchup, taking a 19-0 lead before the Patriots were able to get on the board in the fourth. The Seahawks then kept New England at bay for the remainder of the contest, clinching a championship.

Now, Seattle will look to remain a Super Bowl contender this year following the offseason departures of running back Kenneth Walker III and offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak.

articles.title: Sam Darnold Injured, Latest News on Seahawks QB's Status After Exiting vs. Patriots in Season Opener
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks starting quarterback Sam Darnold suffered a hip injury in the team's season-opening 13-10 win against the New England Patriots and missed the majority of the contest.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks starting quarterback Sam Darnold suffered a hip injury in the team's season-opening 13-10 win against the New England Patriots and missed the majority of the contest.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, Darnold had a CT scan on his hip at Harborview Medical Center in Seattle. The initial test "was encouraging," per Schefter, but it came back inconclusive.

Darnold will undergo an MRI on Thursday.

According to Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald, the team has ruled out a fracture of Darnold's hip.

Darnold appeared to injure his hip on a sack by New England's Dre'Mont Jones in the first quarter. He was replaced by Drew Lock.

Darnold, 29, was fantastic last season during his first year leading the Seahawks, throwing for 4,048 yards, 25 touchdowns and 14 interceptions while completing 67.7 percent of his passes and taking 27 sacks. That earned him Pro Bowl honors for the second straight season.

He was even better in the postseason, throwing for 672 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions in three games as the Seahawks won the Super Bowl.

It was the culmination of a long redemption arc for Darnold, who was the No. 3 overall pick in the 2018 NFL draft by the New York Jets but struggled during his three seasons in the Big Apple.

Two years in Carolina weren't much better for Darnold before a backup gig in San Francisco during the 2023 season—under famed quarterback whisperer Kyle Shanahan—began his turnaround.

He was excellent in 2024 for the Minnesota Vikings, throwing for 4,319 yards, 35 touchdowns and 12 interceptions before a rough outing against the Los Angeles Rams in the Wild Card Round ended that campaign. But he parlayed that success into a three-year, $100 million deal with the Seahawks.

As for Lock, he's an experienced backup who has made 28 starts in his career but has gone just 10-18 in those games with a 34-28 touchdown-to-interception ratio. Suffice to say, any injury to Darnold is a major concern in Seattle as the Seahawks look to defend their title.

articles.title: Courtland Sutton Compares Bo Nix to 'Mountain Lion' Ahead of Broncos Opener vs. Mahomes, Chiefs
articles.summary: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix led his team to a great 2025 season, finishing 14-3, earning the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs, and reaching the conference championship game.
articles.body:
Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix led his team to a great 2025 season, finishing 14-3, earning the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs, and reaching the conference championship game.

Unfortunately, Nix missed the AFC title matchup, a 10-7 home loss to the New England Patriots, after fracturing his ankle the week before against the Buffalo Bills in the divisional round.

Thankfully, Nix is healthy and ready to go, and Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton has taken notice, comparing the signal-caller to a "mountain lion" given his intense desire to return to the field.

"I'm a little nervous for everybody else … he's a competitor now," Sutton said following Wednesday's practice, per ESPN's Jeff Legwold . "He's like that, like a mountain lion in the zoo, that's like pacing. I saw a mountain lion at the Colorado zoo, and he was just pacing back and forth. I was like, 'Y'all don't want that boy to get out, because that's not going to be good.' That's what Bo reminds me of … you can tell he's like, 'I'm ready to go do this.'"

Nix agreed with the assessment, via Legwold.

"Out here [in Colorado], there's different animals you can encounter, [and] I hear a lot of times it's mountain lions and bears you don't want to come across, so I guess that's a good comparison," Nix said. "The thing about mountain lions is usually when you notice them it's because they noticed you a long time ago. I'm just excited to get out there; I feel like I'm pacing, feel like I've been in this practice schedule a long time."

Nix has practiced fully at training camp, but he went through a tough road before then. He underwent surgery a few days after the initial injury to repair the fracture and then had a second surgery in April due to bone spurs.

Per Legwold, Nix did some "limited throwing" at mandatory minicamp in June, but he wasn't a full go until training camp. He made one preseason appearance this year, completing six-of-nine passes for 76 yards.

Nix has become the king of the fourth quarter comeback, engineering eight of them since becoming a starter (2024) and 10 game-winning drives overall. He has been inconsistent and erratic at times, but when the lights are brightest, Nix has produced.

It's easy to feel confident about the Broncos' 2026 season, especially with Nix back under center and Jaylen Waddle now aboard following a trade with the Miami Dolphins.

As for Nix, he won't have to pace like a mountain lion much longer, as he and the Broncos will open the season on Monday evening against the Kansas City Chiefs.

articles.title: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold leaves game with a hip injury in NFL opener
articles.summary: Darnold threw for 4,048 yards and 25 touchdowns last season while leading Seattle to the Super Bowl.
articles.body: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold’s 2026 season debut lasted just one drive before a hip injury knocked out the Super Bowl champion. Darnold injured his right hip, and there is no timetable for his return, the team announced. Facing the New England Patriots in the NFL’s season-opening primetime game — a rematch of February’s Super Bowl — Darnold was playing only his fifth snap when he was sacked on the opening drive and hobbled off the field, though he did not require assistance to reach the sideline. After he was evaluated in a privacy tent on Seattle’s sideline at Lumen Field, he underwent X-rays in the locker room and was listed as questionable, and he was later ruled out for the game. ESPN reported that a CT scan on Darnold’s hip returned “inconclusive” and that he was scheduled for an MRI on Thursday. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that the team had received “great news back” from Darnold’s scan, suggesting that a fracture had been ruled out. Darnold was replaced by backup quarterback Drew Lock, and Seattle’s offense continued to sputter during the first half. Seattle came back to score 13 unanswered points and win the game 13-10. Lock finished with 187 yards and a touchdown while completing 16 of his 22 passes. “I should have given him the game ball,” Macdonald said postgame. “We love Drew. Guys love him. He’s just a Seahawk through and through, man, and it’s like OK, Drew’s in the game, your heart goes out to Sam, we’re praying it’s minor obviously. ... You also want to feel excited for that player and we had a lot of confidence in Drew.” Lock said his focus after he stepped in for Darnold was to “take care of the football. I know what kind of defense we have, the kind of playmakers we have on this side of the ball.” Seattle needed three interceptions of New England’s Drake Maye and eight catches for 122 yards by star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba to pull off its comeback victory. Darnold is one of six active quarterbacks with Super Bowl wins, and he is the only quarterback ever to win a title for his fifth team or later. Last season, he joined Tom Brady (2003-04) as the only quarterbacks in NFL history to win 14 games as a starter in consecutive seasons.

articles.title: “I can have a way better life than this”: How Travis Kelce’s “knucklehead” phase became the turning point that shaped his NFL career with the Chiefs
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is now one of the NFL’s biggest personalities, but the confidence, humour and energy that fans see today came after a period when he had .
articles.body: Travis Kelce is now one of the NFL’s biggest personalities, but the confidence, humour and energy that fans see today came after a period when he had to seriously rethink his life. Before he became a Kansas City Chiefs star, Kelce was dealing with a major setback at Cincinnati and working an $8-an-hour telemarketing job. He has since looked back at that period as the moment he realised he needed to grow up, change his approach and make football count. What followed was a transformation that eventually helped shape the player and personality he is today. Travis Kelce’s $8-an-hour job forced the “knucklehead” to rethink his futureKelce has never tried to pretend that he was perfectly disciplined as a young man. In fact, he has openly referred to himself as a “knucklehead,” and one of the biggest turning points in his life came when football was suddenly taken away from him.In 2010, while at Cincinnati, Kelce lost his scholarship and was away from the football team. Instead of spending his days on the field, he took a telemarketing job where he earned $8 an hour and sat in a small cubicle conducting surveys. ESPN’s Elizabeth Merrill reported that Kelce found the experience depressing because he had spent virtually his entire life playing sports.Looking back at that period for ESPN in 2017, Kelce made an important distinction about the job. He said, “All I had been doing is playing outside, playing sports my entire life. I had never sat down and tried to earn a living like that. That’s not to hit on anybody’s 9-to-5; that’s just not for me.”That experience made him think about what he wanted from his future. Kelce understood that if he wanted football to remain part of his life, he could not keep making the same mistakes.He summed up that realisation with a line that now feels almost like the starting point of his NFL story: “The light at the end of the tunnel was that if I do what I’m supposed to do instead of being a knucklehead, I can have a way better life than this.”That was the change in mindset he needed. Kelce returned to Cincinnati, rebuilt his football career and eventually entered the NFL Draft, where the Chiefs selected him in the third round in 2013. Travis Kelce turned the personality that once got him into trouble into his biggest strengthThe most interesting part of Kelce’s story is that growing up did not mean becoming a completely different person. The personality was always there. He simply learned how to use it in a way that helped rather than hurt him.Ahead of Super Bowl 58 in February 2024, Kelce revealed something that seemed surprising considering how naturally he handles huge crowds and cameras. He said he had actually been a shy kid growing up and credited his mother, Donna Kelce, for helping him become comfortable in front of cameras through the home videos she recorded.Asked how he became so comfortable with a microphone and camera around him, Kelce replied, “My mom’s home videos, man.” He explained that having a camera around him while growing up meant he was constantly seeing himself and getting used to being recorded.But Kelce also pointed to another major source of his confidence: sports. He explained that he was shy until he stepped onto a field, court or ice rink, where he could let his personality come out while having fun and finding success.“Then I kind of let my personality show. I was having fun. I was having success. And that’s just kind of propelled me to have confidence in life,” Kelce said.That helps explain why his old “knucklehead” label is such an important part of his story. Kelce did not lose the playful personality that had been there since childhood. He learned to channel that energy into football, competition and eventually the enormous platform that came with becoming a Chiefs star.The player who once sat in an $8-an-hour telemarketing cubicle wondering where his life was going eventually became one of the most accomplished tight ends of his generation. His journey was not simply about becoming more confident. It was about recognising that he had a future worth fighting for and finally deciding to take it seriously.The “knucklehead” phase was not the end of Travis Kelce’s story. In many ways, it was where his NFL story really began.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL's Week 1 9/11 tribute begins in Seattle with wild guitar solo during national anthem
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks honored 9/11's 25th anniversary with a moment of silence before Pearl Jam's Mike McCready delivered a grunge-style anthem.
articles.body: The NFL promised that its Week 1 games would honor the victims of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks on the 25th anniversary. However, individual teams had some leeway in how they did so, and the Seattle Seahawks took a uniquely local approach. The league’s first game of the 2026 regular season, a rematch of Super Bowl LX between the visiting New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks, featured a pregame announcement that will be heard throughout the league Thursday in Australia, before Sunday’s games and ahead of Monday Night Football: "This weekend marks the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks of September 11th, the deadliest in our nation's history," the Lumens Field announcement bellowed. "We now ask that you join us in a moment of silence in honor of those affected by the September 11th tragedy." A jihadist attack might have been a more accurate description, but we all know what kind of terrorists perpetrated it. Anyway, after the moment of silence, the crowd was directed to both a sign language and guitar solo interpretation of the national anthem. The guitar solo was performed by Pearl Jam's Mike McCready. McCready, a liberal who has advocated all things ObamaCare and former President Obama, started out quite well. It actually kind of hearkened back to Jimi Hendrix's rendition for a minute. And then McCready apparently remembered he's a Seattle grunge rocker and went totally off Francis Scott Key script. "Authentically Seattle," NBC's Mike Tirico noted on NBC. articles.title: “What an odd thing to say”: Mina Kimes slams Aaron Rodgers’ bizarre “pregnant wife” remark while Steelers QB reveals his surprising plans for life after the NFL

articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has already made it clear that the 2026 season will be his last NFL campaign. Yet it was not his retirement decision that caught Mina Kimes’ attention this week. Instead, the ESPN analyst focused on one unusual phrase Rodgers used while discussing what he wants from life once his football career ends.The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback spoke about starting a family with his wife, Brittani, during a SiriusXM Mad Dog Sports Radio interview with Adam Schein. Rodgers’ choice of words quickly became the talking point, particularly because he referred to his future wife as his “pregnant wife.” Mina Kimes found Aaron Rodgers’ “pregnant wife” wording hard to ignoreRecently, Mina Kimes discussed Aaron Rodgers’ comments on “The Sports Gossip Show”. Her reaction was immediate.“I just don't know if I've ever heard anyone use those words in that way,” Kimes said during the show. “That was my reaction. You know the Bart Simpson [quote], ‘What an odd thing to say.’”She then explained why the wording stood out to her. “It was just a strange way of putting it, as opposed to, ‘I want to start a family,’” Kimes added.Rodgers made the original comment during his SiriusXM Mad Dog Sports Radio interview with Adam Schein.“I’m hopefully going to be supporting my pregnant wife because we’re going to start a family and I am not going to be making a lot of appearances or statements,” Rodgers told Schein.There is an important distinction here. Rodgers did not announce that Brittani is currently pregnant. He was describing the family life he hopes to have once his playing career ends. He also said he wants to step away from the constant attention that has followed him throughout his NFL career.“And I’m looking forward to a life of quiet after 22 years in the pros and three in college and getting my body healed up and working on a family. That’s what I’m looking forward to,” Rodgers said during the same interview. Aaron Rodgers’ family plans go beyond one unusual commentAaron Rodgers’ comments fit with several things he has said about his life away from football in recent months.Also, the 42-year-old quarterback announced that the 2026 season would be his final NFL season. He also spoke openly about wanting to become a father and spending more time with his family once football is over. Rodgers has talked about enjoying his role as “Uncle Aaron” while spending time with his nieces and nephews, which has strengthened his desire to have children of his own.His wife Brittani has also played a major role in this new chapter. During a July 28 press conference, Rodgers revealed that he had considered making the previous season his last before the Steelers hired Mike McCarthy. He then spoke with Brittani before deciding to return for one more year.“I talked to the wife, and she said, ‘You can do one more year,’” Rodgers said at the Steelers press conference on July 28.Brittani has also helped Rodgers reconnect with his family after years of estrangement. During an August 1 appearance on NFL Network’s “Good Morning Football”, Rodgers credited her love and support for helping him become open to repairing those relationships.Aaron Rodgers may have attracted attention with one unusual phrase, but his bigger message was clear. The latest update had Brown limping to the locker room, which dimmed his chances of returning. ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport both confirmed the team listed him as questionable with an ankle injury.The timing stings for New England. Brown came to the Patriots in a blockbuster offseason trade, with Philadelphia sending him over for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick, with the Eagles absorbing roughly $43.5 million in dead money across two cap years. This was New England's biggest roster move in years, a clear signal that the franchise is building around Drake Maye right now, not later.Before getting hurt, Brown had three catches for 26 yards, leading the Patriots in receiving. "And they're even higher than expectations I have myself," he said of head coach Mike Vrabel. That mindset was on full display before the injury brought everything to a halt.How does A.J. Brown's ankle injury affect Drake Maye and the Patriots' offense going forward?Even before Brown went down, the Patriots' passing attack was grinding. That was the plan. A multi-week absence would force Maye to operate without his most dangerous receiver during a stretch of the season when rhythm and confidence matter most for a young quarterback still growing into a franchise role.Brown carries serious pedigree into this role. He has 524 career receptions, 8,029 yards, 56 touchdowns, three Pro Bowls, and a Super Bowl ring from his time with the Eagles. He is not just depth. He is the offense's heartbeat. articles.title: Kirk Cousins, Cooper Kupp and Top Fantasy Waiver-Wire Pickups After A.J. Brown, Sam Darnold Injuries
articles.summary: One game into the NFL season, fantasy football players already have reasons to worry. Our anxiety-riddled hobby is back!
articles.body:
One game into the NFL season, fantasy football players already have reasons to worry. Our anxiety-riddled hobby is back!

Sam Darnold left Wednesday's season-opener with a hip injury suffered on the first drive of the game and didn't return. A.J. Brown suffered an ankle injury in the third quarter and also didn't return. Panic ensued.

If you're rostering either player and find yourself already considering other options to pick up on waivers this week, fear not. Chances are you didn't draft Darnold to be your starting quarterback anyway, but having multiple options is always preferable (and obviously this list will probably look very different after the Week 1 games are all played).

Look, Kirk Cousins was awful in his two seasons in Atlanta, he doesn't have many weapons in Las Vegas and his most important target—tight end Brock Bowers—is going to miss at least a game or two after having a meniscus trim.

But at least Cousins has a past pedigree of fantasy relevance, which is more than you are going to get from most of the quarterbacks available on waivers. Darnold certainly looked very good in Klint Kubiak's offense—perhaps Cousins can turn back the clock as well.

Malik Willis is rostered in 41 percent of Yahoo fantasy leagues , so there's a chance he isn't available in your league. If he is, however, he's the guy to pursue from a ceiling perspective.

Yes, he's largely an unknown quantity as a starter, but there's a good chance Miami's entire offense this season is a whole lot of De'Von Achane touches and Willis scrambles. His rushing upside alone makes him an intriguing bet.

Kupp isn't really a long-term option, given his modest 2025 production (47 catches for 593 yards and two touchdowns) and his age (33). Frankly, you are probably only considering him in deeper PPR leagues.

But... in Week 2 he gets the Arizona Cardinals, while in Week 3 he'll face the Washington Commanders. And Drew Lock found him on a few big plays and a touchdown pass that was called back due to an illegal shift.

With more injuries inevitably to follow this weekend, Kupp could end up being a sneaky pick if you need a short-term option given his pending matchups.

Somebody has to pick up some of the slack in the passing game with Bowers hurt. Why not Tre Tucker?

The Las Vegas wideout is only rostered in 30 percent of Yahoo leagues , so there's a good chance he'll be available. That number is going to change dramatically if he shows solid chemistry with Cousins in Week 1. He's very much a player who should be on your radar.

articles.title: Seahawks Beat Patriots, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Drake Maye, JSN as Darnold, Brown Injured
articles.summary: It may have been a costly season-opening victory for the reigning Super Bowl champions, but it was a victory nonetheless.
articles.body:
It may have been a costly season-opening victory for the reigning Super Bowl champions, but it was a victory nonetheless.

The Seattle Seahawks defeated the New England Patriots 13-10 on Wednesday at Lumen Field, although there was plenty of concern from the home team as well considering quarterback Sam Darnold suffered a hip injury .

Drew Lock stepped up in his absence and found Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a critical touchdown in the fourth quarter before driving into field-goal range for what proved to be the winning kick. On the other side, Drake Maye threw three interceptions, the last of which was extremely ill-advised and picked by Josh Jobe in the end zone in the final seconds.

While New England was much closer to defeating Seattle than it was in the Super Bowl, it couldn't overcome Maye's mistakes.

Wednesday figured to be a night of celebration in Seattle as it raised its Super Bowl banner ahead of a rematch against a team it defeated with ease when the Lombardi Trophy was on the line.

However, it didn't take long for concern to take center stage.

Darnold suffered his injury on the home team's opening possession, which paved the way for Lock to take over under center.

It was obvious in the early going the backup was in the game.

Seattle had six first downs to four punts in a scoreless first half as Lock struggled to move the ball against a stout New England defense. On the other side, the Patriots offense didn't have to do much but did score the season's first touchdown when Maye found Eli Raridon for a two-yard score in the second quarter.

It was a pass interference drawn by New England's newest weapon, A.J. Brown., that set up the score, but he was lost for the game when he suffered an ankle injury early in the third quarter.

That wasn't the visitors' only concern, as Seattle finally got on the board with a field goal after an incredible catch by Cooper Kupp before Nehemiah Pritchett picked off Maye to swing momentum fully to the Seahawks' side despite a 10-3 deficit in the fourth quarter.

It was also only a matter of time before Smith-Njigba made his presence known, and the Ohio State product swung the game when he hauled in a short pass on 4th-and-1 and then exploded through New England's defense for a 45-yard touchdown to tie it.

From there, Romeo Doubs had a brutal drop before Maye threw another interception, this time to Julian Love. His second pick set up a go-ahead field goal for Seattle, although Lock's inability to convert ideal field position into a touchdown meant the Patriots were down just three.

That gave Maye the opportunity to be a hero, but he threw the game-clinching interception instead.

Every NFL season is different. The Seattle Seahawks found out rather quickly during the 2027 campaign's opening contest.

The defending Super Bowl champs had their starting quarterback, Sam Darnold, for a total of five plays during Wednesday's season-opener against the New England Patriots—which saw a completely different outcome than what occurred during Super Bowl LX. The latest campaign looks drastically different already, and it just began.

Check back throughout the weekend as Bleacher Report's team of NFL analysts break down each contest and provide takeaways from all of the action.

New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks

Can Seahawks Continue Winning Ways with Drew Lock at QB?

The answer seems fairly obvious after Wednesday's performance. Lock was fairly efficient and didn't make any major mistakes after taking over for Sam Darnold, who was ruled out of the contest thanks to an injured hip.

If the veteran backup is forced to serve as QB1 for an extended period, he'll eventually make mistakes and show the same erratic play seen throughout his seven-year career. However, Seattle has the luxury to lean on an established offensive line, talented running game, standout wide receivers and a top-notch defense. As a result, Lock is good enough to help the Seahawks win plenty of game if necessary.

Seattle's Defense Picks Up Where It Left Off, Which is Scary for Rest of NFL

The Seahawks defense isn't the same today as the unit that dominated during Super Bowl LX, but the group can still dictate a contest.

Riq Woolen, Coby Bryant and Boye Mafe left in free agency. Their absences were barely felt, if at all. Furthermore, safeties Nick Emmanwori and Ty Okada weren't in the lineup due to injuries. Yet Seattle still allowed fewer than 300 yards at 4.1 yards per play. Plus, the group created three turnovers.

A three-interception outing isn't always the worst thing. In Maye's case, he couldn't have made worse decisions, which led to three turnovers.

Last season, the MVP runner-up emerged as one of the game's best deep-ball throwers . Seattle's secondary read Maye like a book, particularly when he wanted to push the ball down the field. He forced all three passes that led to the takeaways, while throwing the game away with under 30 seconds left in regulation despite the Patriots being in makeable field-goal range. How Big Is AJ Brown's Injury to Patriots' Offense? Part of Maye's problem stems from the fact his new WR1 left the contest and didn't return. Brown caught three passes for 26 yards in his Patriots debut. Unfortunately, the veteran target suffered what appeared to be an ankle injury. Brown can be a physically dominate X-receiver in New England's offense. Without him for any period of time, the Patriots once again find themselves in a place where the unit lacks a consistent threat on the outside.

The NFL's 2027 International Series opens in Melbourne when the San Francisco 49ers meet the rival Los Angeles Rams. It's the league's first contest in Australia. The reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, will make his debut with the Rams. Though Los Angeles' defensive front will be without Aaron Donald.

A total of 13 games will be played during the first Sunday of the 2027 campaign. Each matchup is intriguing at some level. However, Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen facing the Houston Texans' ferocious defense has to be the biggest showdown.

Less than nine months ago, Patrick Mahomes suffered a torn ACL. The two-time NFL MVP will be in the lineup Monday against the Denver Broncos. Will he be the same Mahomes, though? Denver's standout defense will find out sooner rather than later.

articles.title: Sam Darnold ruled out with hip injury after only one drive, replaced by Drew Lock in Seahawks win
articles.summary: Sam Darnold was sacked and suffered a leg injury early in Wednesday's game.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks ' celebration over raising their Super Bowl banner and the start of a new season didn't last long Wednesday.

Quarterback Sam Darnold left the season-opening game against the New England Patriots after one series due to a hip injury. He was replaced by Drew Lock . Darnold went back to the locker room with athletic trainers before the Seahawks' second series started.

Late in the second quarter, Darnold was ruled out by the Seahawks for the rest of the game. After a slow start, Lock and Seattle made just enough plays to pull off a dramatic 13-10 win .

Darnold was not at the stadium for the rest of the game. He went to nearby Harborview Medical Center for a CT scan on his hip, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter . That test came back inconclusive, and he's set to undergo an MRI on Thursday. The Seahawks did rule out a hip fracture, but further specifics on his injury are not yet known.

Lock finished 16 of 22 for 187 yards passing and a 45-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba .

On the play he was hurt, Darnold was sacked by Patriots end Dre'Mont Jones on a third down on the Seahawks' first drive. As the punt team came on, Darnold was trotting off with a noticeable limp. NBC said on the broadcast that no medical personnel was around Darnold as he came to the sideline, but shortly after he went to the blue medical tent.

After the Patriots punted, NBC showed Darnold limping badly on the sideline as Lock had his helmet on, ready to go in.

Darnold didn't miss a game last season and threw for 4,000 yards in the regular season, then played steady, solid football throughout the Seahawks' Super Bowl championship push. He became a great story of a highly drafted quarterback who was given up on by multiple teams.

As a new season started, another story was unfolding and it wasn't a positive one for the Seahawks or Darnold.

articles.title: Drake Maye Addresses Late INT That Sealed Seahawks Win vs. Patriots in NFL Season Opener
articles.summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions during his team's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Wednesday's season opener, but it was the final one in the end zone to Josh Jobe that stood out the most.
articles.body:
New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions during his team's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Wednesday's season opener, but it was the final one in the end zone to Josh Jobe that stood out the most.

"Didn't put enough on it," Maye told reporters. "… It was just unacceptable. We have a chance to send it to overtime at the worst, and the only thing you can't do is turn the ball over."

He also said he "lost patience and cost us."

While the Patriots let a 10-0 lead slip away in the second half, they were still in ideal position on their final drive.

After all, the defense just held Seattle to a field goal and gave Maye the ball back with the chance to score the winning touchdown in the final moments. By the time he converted his second fourth-down attempt of the drive, it seemed like the visitors were going to find the end zone.

The interception came after the Patriots drove into the red zone, making it all the more difficult to accept considering a field goal would have forced overtime.

It wasn't the only late mistake for Maye, who threw three interceptions in the fourth quarter alone after struggling to consistently move the ball against Seattle's stout defense for much of the game.

That allowed the Seahawks to come back even though they were playing without quarterback Sam Darnold, who suffered a hip injury during their first possession and never returned. It wasn't the only notable injury, as Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown also exited with a setback.

With Brown not on the field during those fourth-quarter drives, Maye threw the critical interceptions and opened the door for the Seahawks to come back and start the season with a win.

Maye and the Patriots will look to bounce back in Week 2 when they face the Pittsburgh Steelers at home.

articles.title: Romeo Doubs Reacts to Brutal Drop in Patriots' Loss vs. Seahawks, 'Video Speaks for Itself'
articles.summary: New England Patriots wide receiver Romeo Doubs discussed his costly drop in the fourth quarter of the team's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
New England Patriots wide receiver Romeo Doubs discussed his costly drop in the fourth quarter of the team's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday night.

"I just wasn't locked in enough," Doubs said after the game, per Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald . "That's all. Video speaks for itself. And like I said, I'll be better."

With the score tied 10-10 in the fourth quarter, Doubs dropped a pass from Drake Maye that would have given the Patriots a first down.

On New England's next play, Maye was picked off while attempting to move the chains.

Doubs was targeted three times against Seattle, but failed to record a catch.

His fourth-quarter drop as well as Maye's interception allowed the Seahawks to take a 13-10 lead.

The Patriots drove down to Seattle's 16-yard line on their final drive of the game, but Maye was picked off again with just over 20 seconds left in the fourth to seal the final result.

As for Doubs, his Patriots debut was underwhelming after signing a four-year contract worth $68 million with the team in free agency.

He wrapped up a productive 2025 campaign with the Green Bay Packers before joining New England, hauling in 55 receptions for a career-high 724 yards while scoring six touchdowns in 16 games.

Doubs also dropped just three passes on 85 targets last season (via Pro Football Reference ).

He continued to make plays throughout his first Patriots training camp as well.

New England will be hoping that he can bounce back quickly, especially after star wideout A.J. Brown exited Wednesday's contest in the third quarter after suffering an ankle injury .

If Brown misses time moving forward, Doubs should receive plenty of opportunities to make up for his season-opening performance.

articles.title: Who are Drew Lock’s parents? Meet Andy and Laura Lock, the family behind the Seattle Seahawks QB
articles.summary: NFL News: Drew Lock has stepped back into the spotlight for the Seattle Seahawks after Sam Darnold was ruled out with a hip injury during the season opener agai.
articles.body: Drew Lock has stepped back into the spotlight for the Seattle Seahawks after Sam Darnold was ruled out with a hip injury during the season opener against the Patriots. Lock entered the game as Seattle’s backup quarterback and took over for Darnold. But behind his long football journey are two people who have been there from the beginning: his parents, Andy and Laura Lock.Both of Drew’s parents had sporting backgrounds of their own, and they played a major role in helping him develop as an athlete and as a person. While Andy had experience as a college football player, Laura was a standout basketball player who later worked in education.Who are Drew Lock’s parents, Andy and Laura Lock?Drew was born in Columbia, Missouri, on November 10, 1996, and grew up in Lee’s Summit. He was raised by Andy and Laura on their 10-acre family homestead, where sports became a big part of his childhood.Andy had played offensive tackle for the Missouri Tigers from 1986 to 1989. He went undrafted after college but received an opportunity to attend New York Giants training camp after his playing career at Missouri. His football career did not last long, but he later built a career in business. A LinkedIn profile previously cited in reporting listed Andy as a regional manager with the McCormick and Schmidt’s franchise in Lee’s Summit from 2005.Laura grew up in Centralia, Missouri, and was a star high school basketball player. She later worked as a teacher and school administrator. Her own experience in sports helped her understand the demands placed on a young athlete, although she was also closely involved in Drew’s life away from competition.Andy and Laura met at a bank in Columbia. Laura was working there as a teller when Andy came in to make deposits for a restaurant where he was working after his time with the Giants. Their meeting eventually led to marriage and the birth of Drew and his sister Claire.Laura has recalled how athletic Drew was from a very young age. He played basketball, baseball and other sports while growing up, and his parents encouraged him to develop his abilities without becoming too focused on his own success.How Drew Lock’s parents supported him throughout his NFL journeyLaura was one of Drew’s biggest supporters, particularly when he faced criticism. During the 2020 COVID-19 controversy involving the Denver Broncos, she publicly defended her son and explained that Drew and the quarterback room had asked for permission to watch film at the team facility.Drew later described his mother as a “fiery” person and acknowledged that she would always stand up for him. He also joked about how strongly she reacted when he did not play well.His parents were equally emotional supporters during his college career at Missouri. Laura admitted that watching Drew take hits as a freshman was difficult for her. She recalled sitting in the stands, covering her eyes and hoping he would get back up. After games, Drew would reassure her that he was fine.The quarterback has also spoken about how much it meant to have Andy and Laura attend his games. After one of his early NFL victories, Lock said, “It means the world to me that they end up coming to all these games for me.” He added that they had supported him throughout college and would continue trying to do the same in the NFL.Laura also tried to keep Drew humble as his football career grew. She encouraged him to be thankful for his abilities and to help the people around him rather than boasting about his own achievements.Now, with Lock back on the field for Seattle, his parents remain an important part of the story behind the quarterback. Andy gave him an understanding of the highs and disappointments of football, while Laura provided the constant support and encouragement that followed him from childhood to the NFL.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
