articles.title: 49ers stars Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle and Nick Bosa all cleared to play vs. Rams in Australia
articles.summary: The 49ers and Rams are relatively healthy after all entering their matchup in Australia.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers released their final injury report of the week before Thursday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams , and their biggest names are apparently good to go after all.

While running back Christian McCaffrey , edge rusher Nick Bosa and George Kittle were limited during the preseason, none of the three star players have an injury designation heading into Thursday's game against the Rams in Australia (8:35 p.m. ET, Netflix). McCaffrey wasn't listed on the 49ers' injury report, while both Bosa and Kittle had "limited participation" at practice this week. Neither of them had an injury designation for the game.

McCaffrey was limited during the preseason and was reportedly dealing with general tightness. This, of course, sparked fears in fans who remember the 2024 season, when he had been listed as questionable with a calf issue for Week 1, then ended up being a surprise inactive and then played in only four games that season.

Bosa and Kittle weren't recovering from preseason injuries, but rather from season-ending injuries from 2025. Bosa tore his right ACL in Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals and has been dealing with tendinitis. Kittle being off the injury report is the most shocking. The tight end tore his right Achilles in last season's playoffs. Kittle suffered his injury Jan. 11, but appears to be ready to gear up against the Rams eight months later.

McCaffrey avoided the injury report the entire week. Both Kittle and Bosa were included but were listed as limited during Tuesday's and Wednesday's practices.

After playing in only four games in 2024, McCaffrey returned last season and was fully healthy. He played in all 17 games and ran for 1,202 yards with 10 touchdowns on the ground and added 924 yards and seven additional scores through the air. These stats helped him earn the 2025 NFL Comeback Player of the Year Award.

The 28-year-old Bosa is entering his eighth season with the 49ers. Before his injury last year, he had played in three games and had tallied 17 tackles, including two sacks.

The best season of his career came in 2022 when he earned the Defensive Player of the Year Award. Bosa played in 16 games and had a career-high 18.5 sacks.

Kittle is heading into his 10th NFL season, all with San Francisco. He played in 11 games last season and had 628 yards with seven touchdowns. Kittle, despite being 32 years old, remains one of the best tight ends in the league.

The only player ruled out for the 49ers is defensive lineman Alfred Collins , who was r uled out for the season earlier this week with a knee injury . Meanwhile, defensive tackle James Thompson is listed as questionable with a hamstring injury.

The Rams are all clear on their injury report. The only player listed as out was Aaron Donald , but he didn't make the trip to Australia. He is still ramping back up after he came out of retirement to rejoin the Rams late last month.

articles.title: Seattle Seahawks beat New England Patriots after Drake Maye's three interceptions and Sam Darnold injury in NFL season-opener
articles.summary: Drake Maye throws three costly interceptions in the final quarter as the Seattle Seahawks beat the New England Patriots in a rematch of February's Super Bowl to raise the curtain on the 2026 NFL season; Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is injured on the opening drive
articles.body:
The Seahawks were held to just a field goal through three quarters as Lock and the offense struggled to move the ball after Darnold injured his hip on the opening drive.

But the costly interceptions by last season's MVP runner-up turned the tide and ensured the opening night of the 2026 NFL campaign would end in happy fashion for the home Seattle crowd.

Maye overcame the first two picks to drive the Patriots into position to tie or take the lead in the final minute. But Josh Jobe made a toe-tapping interception in the end zone to seal the win.

Passing: Drake Maye, 23/33, 178 yards, 1 TD, 3 INTs

Rushing: Rhamondre Stevenson, 18 carries, 51 yards

Receiving: Mack Hollins, 4 catches, 51 yards

Passing: Drew Lock, 16/22, 187 yards, 1 TD

Rushing: Jadarian Price, 10 carries, 52 yards

Receiving: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, 8 catches, 122 yards, 1 TD

Seattle trailed 10-0 but got a field goal in the third quarter and tied the game when Lock connected with Jaxon Smith-Njigba on a 45-yard pass on fourth-and-one following an interception by Nehemiah Pritchett.

Julian Love intercepted Maye on the next drive and the Seahawks took a 13-10 lead on a 26-yard field goal by Jason Myers. That set the stage for the defensive stand on the final drive.

The game started following a ceremony that featured the Super Bowl banner being raised and highlights being played on the video board. This was the third Super Bowl rematch in Week One with it last happening in 2016 when Denver celebrated its title with a win over Carolina.

The excitement turned to worry quickly as Darnold came up limping following a third-down sack by Dre'Mont Jones on the first drive. Darnold went immediately to the sideline medical tent and then back to the locker room before the next drive.

Lock, who threw just three passes last season, entered the game but Seattle's offense was stagnant until the fourth quarter.

The Patriots didn't fare much better on offense but got the only score of the first half after Jobe interfered with offseason acquisition A.J. Brown on a deep flea-flicker pass and Maye found rookie Eli Raridon for a two-yard score on the next play to make it 7-0.

A penalty helped set up the second Patriots score as well. Chazz Surratt was flagged for roughing the punter on the opening drive of the second half, setting up Andy Borregales' 50-yard field goal.

Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said after the game Darnold did not break any bones following the hip injury sustained on the opening drive.

"At this point we were able to rule out a fracture," he said, before calling the initial diagnosis "positive".

Darnold didn't miss a game last season while throwing for 4,048 yards, 25 touchdowns and 14 interceptions on the way to winning the Super Bowl.

The 2018 No 3 overall pick signed with Seattle last offseason having resurrected his NFL career with the Minnesota Vikings the previous year.

"It's tough losing (Darnold). I mean, he's the head of the snake, but we have each other's backs," said wide receiver Smith-Njigba.

"We fully trust in Drew Lock to come in and do his thing, done it time and time again. So we just have to have each other's backs."

Patriots quarterback Maye was critical of his late mistakes in what would become his first career three-interception game.

Maye had converted two fourth downs to lead the Patriots into red zone territory late in the game, before failing to find intended target Mack Hollins on third-and-five from the 16-yard line as Jobe positioned himself for a conclusive interception.

"I was trying to get rid of it, and I realised Mack was back there in the back and I didn't put enough on it to get it out," Maye said. "It was unacceptable.

"I stopped being patient. That was the big thing. We were really good up until the point I tried to force one down the side to Romeo. We were patient and dumping it off and trying to move the chains and we avoided a lot of three-and-outs and that was something we tried, you know just earn more plays and the points will come.

"So I just stopped being patient and made decisions that ended up costing us the game."

articles.title: NFL in Australia: Why are Los Angeles Rams playing San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne?
articles.summary: The NFL has so far played regular-season games in seven international countries but this week's trip to Australia represents a new frontier for the USA's biggest sports league.
articles.body:
The NFL has so far played regular-season games in seven international countries but this week's trip to Australia represents a new frontier.

It is the NFL's first game in the Asia-Pacific region. The USA's biggest sports league is making its longest-ever road trip for the first of a record nine international games in 2026.

It will take place about 10,000 miles from the NFL's New York headquarters, in front of about 100,000 fans at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground.

That means the Los Angeles Rams will 'host' the San Francisco 49ers on a more open oval field on Friday (01:35 BST).

But when NFL commissioner Roger Goodell visited the MCG for the first time in April, he said the historic arena "speaks to you", and it says "this is the right place to be".

American football is coming to Australia - can it succeed?

Live NFL games have been broadcast in Australia since 1995 and a pre-season exhibition game was held in Sydney in 1999.

Local interest has soared since 2022, though, when the NFL made the global growth of American football a strategic priority.

The league pivoted away from a potential overseas franchise to playing more games internationally. It has invested in new markets before deciding whether to take a game there, holding year-round events to build the fanbase.

Australian players Jordan Mailata (Philadelphia) and Michael Dickson (Seattle) have also captured the imagination down under, playing for the past two Super Bowl winners.

According to the league, the number of fans in Australia has nearly doubled since 2022 to 8.8 million - almost one in three of the country's entire population.

That includes those flooding to one of the world's fastest-growing sports, flag football - the non-contact version of American football.

The NFL played a big part in flag being approved for its Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028 and has expanded the sport from 10 schools in Australia to more than 500.

Now it aims to help flag football secure a spot at Brisbane 2032, with NFL executive Peter O'Reilly acknowledging that is a key reason for playing in Australia.

Being a sports-mad country, Australia was always on the NFL's radar, and after testing long-distance logistics with trips to Brazil in 2024 and 2025, the league felt ready to head down under.

Sydney and Perth were in the running but Melbourne is regarded as the nation's sports capital and the MCG is the biggest stadium in the southern hemisphere.

A deal was announced in February 2025, during Super Bowl week, and while some fans expressed anger at ticket prices when they went on sale in April 2026, they sold out in minutes.

The state of Victoria is reportedly paying up to A$15m , external (£8m) for the right to host the game but expects one of the state's biggest returns. Dublin enjoyed a tenfold return on its investment to stage its first NFL game last September.

Almost 50% of the MCG tickets were bought by fans outside Victoria or overseas, so about 50,000 fans will visit Melbourne this week.

'The G' is also right next to Melbourne Park, home of tennis' Australian Open, an ideal venue for a three-day fan festival, which began with a watch party for last night's season opener.

The NFL picked this year's Super Bowl week to announce that the 49ers will be the Rams' opponents in Melbourne, which created a buzz in Australia and California.

Not only are the Rams and 49ers regular Super Bowl contenders but they are also divisional rivals in the ultra-competitive NFC West. In addition, there is heaps of hype around the Rams.

With this season's Super Bowl being held in LA, they have gone all-in to reach the big game. First they traded for defensive stars Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie, which cemented them as championship favourites.

Then three-time defensive player of the year Aaron Donald returned from retirement and although the 35-year-old has not travelled to Australia, Garrett and McDuffie will both make their Rams debut at the MCG.

Fred Warner, Nick Bosa and George Kittle are set to return from injury for the 49ers, with Mike Evans making his debut.

The game will be broadcast live on Netflix, reaching more than 200 countries, while the Jonas Brothers will perform a half-time show.

Who will reach Super Bowl? - NFL predictions for 2026 season

California is 17 hours behind Melbourne and the flight takes about 16 hours. The previous longest for a regular-season game was about 12 hours to Sao Paulo, Brazil.

Yet the two teams have taken a completely different approach. The 49ers arrived in Melbourne last Friday while the Rams arrived the day before the game - just as they did for last year's comfortable win at Wembley over the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The huge time difference means that the game kicks off at 10:35 on Friday in Melbourne - which is Thursday evening in the United States: 17:35 on the west coast, 20:35 on the east.

While a morning start (local time) is virtually unheard of in the NFL, it's perfectly normal for fans used to watching cricket at the MCG.

The long flights and early start have thrown each teams' regular routine out of kilter. San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan admitted he was struggling to remember what day it was.

But having the game in week one gives each team the best chance to cope with the travel demands, rather than playing it later in the season.

Kelce's last dance? Five things to look out for in new NFL season

The NFL has committed to playing one more game in Melbourne in the next three years, with the possibility of another.

What sets Australia apart from other countries hosting international games is that ball-carrying sports are the most popular down under.

All seven Australians in the NFL converted from rugby, basketball or Australian rules football, and Australia has a huge pool of similar athletes with transferable skills.

The NFL has pledged to provide flag football kits to every school in Australia and opened an academy on the Gold Coast as it aims to tap into that talent, which could produce an international pipeline of players targeting the Olympics and the NFL.

articles.title: Where is 49ers vs. Rams being played? Location, stadium details and more for 2026 NFL Australia game
articles.summary: Here's a look at where the 49ers and Rams will be playing the their Week 1 contest.
articles.body:
As the NFL opens the 2026 season, the league is taking its international game to a new level for a divisional matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams .

The two NFC West rivals will play a crucial regular-season game 18.5 hours away in Australia, the longest that any team has traveled to play a professional football game. While this is new to NFL teams, the location and stadium are as historic a sports venue as there is in the world.

While the game will kick off at night in the United States, the local time will be early Friday morning, giving teams a chance to play in the bright Australian sun. As a result, NFL fans should be able to get a full sense of this Australian stadium.

Here's a look at where the 49ers and Rams will be playing their Week 1 contest.

The 49ers and Rams are playing the first-ever NFL game in Australia, which will take place at Melbourne Cricket Ground. The stadium is located in East Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, and is one of the most iconic venues not only in Australia, but in the entire world.

Melbourne Cricket Ground in East Melbourne, Victoria, Australia is one of the oldest sports stadiums in the world, as it was first established in 1853. Known locally as the "G", Melbourne Cricket has hosted many of the world's best sporting events, including the Olympics, World Cup qualifiers, and the Commonwealth Games, and it plays host to the Australian Rules Football Grand Final each year.

The Victoria State Government owns the stadium and appoints a select group of people to manage the grounds through the MCG Trust. The stadium has featured renovations twice in its existence, once in 1992 and again in 2006, and could undergo another renovation in 2032.

Melbourne Cricket Ground is home to several teams across a handful of sports in Australia. In Australian Rules Football, Collingwood, Hawthorn, Melbourne and Richmond all play home games at the stadium, while the Australia National Cricket team, the Victoria Cricket team and a few Melbourne cricket teams play their cricket matches there as well.

The stadium also hosts soccer matches for both the Australian men's and women's national teams, and the Melbourne Storm play their home Rugby matches there as well.

articles.title: Surprise option emerges as Bills' top punt returner for Week 1
articles.summary: The Bills spent all summer searching for a punt returner. A new addition has emerged as the leading option ahead of Sunday's opener.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills spent all summer looking for a punt returner.

Dee Alford is listed atop the punt-returner spot on Buffalo's first unofficial depth chart ahead of Sunday's season opener against the Houston Texans .

Ray Davis is listed second and Khalil Shakir third.

It's the clearest indication yet of where Buffalo's wide-open competition stands after the Bills spent training camp and the preseason cycling through options.

At various points during training camp, Keon Coleman , Mecole Hardman , Dante Pettis and Skyler Bell were among the other players fielding punts.

Davis made the Pro Bowl as a return specialist last season after taking over kickoff-return duties midway through the year. He led the NFL with 30.4 yards per kickoff return and remains listed as Buffalo's No. 1 kick returner.

But Davis' audition on punts included a costly mistake.

He muffed a punt in Buffalo's preseason finale against the Pittsburgh Steelers , and the Steelers recovered it at the Bills' 13-yard line. Pittsburgh capitalized off the turnover, scoring a touchdown one play later. General manager Brandon Beane acknowledged the mistake when discussing the unsettled job after roster cuts.

"I can't tell you who's going to line up Week 1 yet," Beane said Sept. 1.

The veteran cornerback isn't new to returning punts. Alford handled 20 of them for the Atlanta Falcons in 2023.

Shakir also has experience. He returned 16 punts for 124 yards last season, averaging 7.8 yards per return.

There's another intriguing option who isn't listed on the depth chart.

Buffalo signed veteran return specialist Greg Dortch to its practice squad Aug. 31. Dortch averaged 11.6 yards on 16 punt returns for the Arizona Cardinals last season, ranking 11th in the NFL.

That would represent a significant improvement for Buffalo. The Bills averaged only 6.5 yards on 30 punt returns last season, ranking 28th in the NFL.

Dortch isn't on the 53-man roster and therefore isn't listed on the depth chart. But Buffalo could elevate him from the practice squad on game day or sign him to the active roster if the Bills eventually decide he's their best option.

Alford could already have plenty on his plate.

The free-agent addition is listed as Buffalo's starting nickel cornerback and the backup to Christian Benford at one of the outside cornerback spots.

The Bills haven't necessarily answered who will be standing underneath Houston's first punt Sunday. But after an entire summer of auditions, they've provided their clearest answer yet.

articles.title: Steelers news: Cam Heyward doesn't hold back about 'stupid' franchise tag
articles.summary: Cam Heyward has never been shy about speaking his mind. The Pittsburgh Steelers captain delivered another blunt assessment ahead of the 2026 season opener ag...
articles.body:
Cam Heyward has never been shy about speaking his mind. The Pittsburgh Steelers captain delivered another blunt assessment ahead of the 2026 season opener against the Atlanta Falcons . Speaking after practice, the veteran defensive tackle and NFLPA executive committee member labeled the NFL's franchise tag "stupid." He argued that the mechanism gives teams too much control over players' careers and earning power.

"It hampers palyers. Why should any team be able to take advantage of a player for one year? It's used in negotiations," Heyward said. "And I think between the player options, the franchise tags, the way they control rookies, I think it's kind of backwards."

His comments come as Pittsburgh approaches a familiar contract deadline. The Steelers traditionally stop negotiations once the regular season begins. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr is entering the final year of his contract . That adds another layer to the team's business decisions.

Entering his 16th NFL season, Heyward remains Pittsburgh's longest-tenured active player. He is their defensive anchor and among their most influential voices. The six-time Pro Bowler and 2023 Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year continues to provide power against the run. His disruptive interior pressure helps lead a defense in transition. His veteran presence will be particularly important alongside Keeanu Benton and Derrick Harmon as the Steelers pursue a high-stakes campaign.

With Aaron Rodgers entering what is expected to be his final NFL season, Pittsburgh is aiming to make a deep postseason push. For Heyward, however, the mission extends beyond Week 1. He wants the Steelers to chase another Lombardi Trophy while continuing to challenge an NFL system he believes too often leaves players without enough leverage.

articles.title: ‘Sore loser’ – NFL fans tear into Mike Vrabel after what he did following Patriots loss
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks got their 2026 season underway with another victory over Mike Vrabel and the New England Patriots. Months on from their Super Bowl in Sa...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks got their 2026 season underway with another victory over Mike Vrabel and the New England Patriots .

Months on from their Super Bowl in Santa Clara, it was another win for Mike Macdonald over Vrabel, with fans believing they noticed something distasteful between the two after the game.

It is routine for the two head coaches and quarterbacks to sprint into the middle of the field at the end of the game to shake hands.

However, there were a number of NFL fans watching the opening game of the season who felt that Vrabel ran straight towards the locker room.

The broadcast did appear to show Vrabel avoid the field after the game ended following Drake Maye 's third interception, with fans coming down heavily on the Patriots HC.

NFL fans criticise Patriots HC Mike Vrabel for avoiding Mike Macdonald handshake

Despite playing almost the entire game without Sam Darnold at quarterback, the Seahawks managed to find a way to come out of Week One with a win.

It would be fair to say that Macdonald has Vrabel's number following back-to-back victories over the 51-year-old.

To not shake Macdonald's hand, which many feel Vrabel avoided, has naturally not gone down well online.

'Wait… did Vrabel just walk off the field without shaking hands? Am I tripping?' said one fan on X after the game ended.

'Did Macdonald and Vrabel shake hands or did Vrabel just run off? Lol,' another fan questioned.

Although there does not appear to be any conclusive answer, the broadcast footage certainly made it look like Vrabel ran in the opposite direction to Macdonald.

One fan took to X and said: 'Did Vrabel not shake hands??'

'I thought I saw the same thing. He was in that tunnel too fast to have,' another fan replied.

It has not been a quiet offseason of preparation for Vrabel, who has been battling the allegations with Dianna Russini.

He has not done himself any favours here, though.

'Did Vrabel not shake Macdonald Seahawks hand? Sure looked like it.. sore loser..' added another NFL fan online.

'Did Vrabel even shake Macdonald's hand. I thought I saw him with his tail tucked leading the pack to the locker room before the clock even said 0. Did I see it wrong?!' said another.

articles.title: NFL: Seattle Seahawks 13-10 New England Patriots - champions win season opener
articles.summary: Defending champions the Seattle Seahawks come from behind to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the opening game of the NFL season.
articles.body:
Defending champions the Seattle Seahawks came from behind to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the opening game of the NFL season.

For the first time in 10 years the season began with a rematch of the Super Bowl, in which the Patriots were dominated by a Seahawks defence known as 'the Dark Side'.

Again they stepped up after Seattle lost quarterback Sam Darnold to a hip injury in the game's opening drive, claiming three interceptions in the final quarter at Lumen Field.

The Patriots went into a 10-0 lead, with rookie tight end Eli Raridon scoring the first touchdown of the season in the second quarter.

Back-up quarterback Drew Lock got the Seattle offence going late in the third quarter, with Jason Myers cutting the gap with a field goal.

Seahawks cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett claimed his first career interception at the start of the fourth quarter, after a Drake Maye pass was deflected by rookie Rodney Thomas.

On the next possession Lock found wide reciever Jaxon Smith-Njigba in space and last season's offensive player of the year charged through the Patriots defence for a 45-yard touchdown.

Julian Love then picked off Patriots quarterback Maye, giving Myers the chance to edge the Seahawks in front with a 26-yard field goal.

New England were well within field-goal range with 21 seconds remaining, but chose to go for the win rather than settle for overtime, and the move backfired as Maye's hopeful pass towards Mack Hollins was intercepted by Josh Jobe in the end zone.

The only game in which Maye threw multiple interceptions last season was the Super Bowl, and he was picked off on the Patriots' final three possessions in the season opener.

Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald said initial tests showed Darnold had not fractured a hip.

Week one continues with the NFL's first regular-season game in Australia. The Los Angeles Rams meet the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne on Thursday (01:35 BST, Friday).

articles.title: Why Jonas Brothers are performing halftime show at NFL Australia game
articles.summary: The Jonas Brothers are lending their world-renowned vocals and musical stylings to the 49ers and Rams' Week 1 tilt in Melbourne. Here's why.
articles.body:
Netflix sought out familiar faces — and voices — to lead its first broadcast of the 2026 NFL season.

The producers that brought viewers halftime show performances by Beyonce and Mariah Carey have another entry in their glistening list. Unlike the others, this one will take place internationally.

With that, here's what you need to know about Netflix and the NFL's joint decision to seek out beloved pop group Jonas Brothers to offer their musical stylings when the 49ers and Rams lock horns down under.

Why Jonas Brothers are performing during the 49ers vs. Rams?

Halftime performances have rarely been a staple in early-season fixtures. Thursday's matchup between San Francisco and Los Angeles stands in stark contrast, by comparison. The league enlisted the Jonas Brothers to soundtrack the second game of the Week 1 slate, hoping to kick off the season with a flourish.

The pop band might appear to be a curious choice at first glance; they hail from neither San Francisco nor Los Angeles, instead emerging from New Jersey's glistening shores. That's more than 10,000 miles away from Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, the site of San Francisco and Los Angeles' Thursday "night" tilt. Social media has made us more connected than ever. And yet, the gulf between the Jonas Brothers' home base and the second-most populous city in Australia appears a little too large to comprehend.

The explanation for the trio's appearance at Melbourne Cricket Ground is far simpler than it may initially appear. They are quite popular, collecting one Grammy, 51 No. 1 placements on the Billboard charts and millions of record sales. That appears to have been enough to coax the league to give the brotherly trio a chance to spearhead the match's mid-game spectacle.

"We couldn't be more excited to perform at halftime during the NFL's first-ever regular season game in Australia," The Jonas Brothers said in a statement to the NFL . "Playing at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground in front of such passionate Australian fans is an incredible honor. We can't wait to be part of this historic moment and celebrate with everyone in the stadium and watching around the world."

What time is 49ers vs. Rams halftime show?

Kickoff from 49ers vs. Rams is slated to take place at 8:35 p.m. ET (5:35 p.m. PT/10:35 a.m. AEST). The NFL hasn't listed an official start time for the halftime show; it will be left to chance, only starting after the players have disappeared into the locker room at halftime.

Ultimately, one will have to proceed with caution when figuring out when The Jonas Brothers will take the stage. Game state will determine when the halftime whistle is blown. The more points and possessions that take place during the first half, the more likely it is that the halftime show will stretch later into the night.

A reasonable estimate for the start of the Jonas Brothers' halftime show appears to be between 10:45-11:-- p.m. ET. It typically takes around two hours for a half to conclude, although the length of the opening two periods — and the time it takes to set up the stage at Melbourne Cricket Ground — could lengthen things.

articles.title: As Patriots fail to overcome loss of A.J. Brown, Drake Maye admits: ‘I just stopped being patient’
articles.summary: There was a sense the Patriots know what they need to do next even if questions linger on how they will do it and how soon Brown will rejoin them.
articles.body:
SEATTLE — In the final four minutes of the 2026 NFL season's opening game, Drake Maye had already scrambled to his right to convert on fourth down.

He'd already found veteran receiver Mack Hollins 11 yards underneath for another fourth down.

And Maye had kept the series alive on third-and-1 with still another fake handoff and wheel around his left to pick up 6 yards.

So when the New England Patriots faced third-and-5 from the Seattle Seahawks ' 16-yard line with 26 seconds to play, down 3, Maye knew logically that all he needed to do was not turn the ball over. He knew logically that he should try to move the chains but try even harder to maintain the possession and chance to send the game to overtime with a chip-shot field goal. Instead the playmaker in him, that superhero tendency quarterbacks so often have to fight, threatened to overtake logic.

Veteran edge rusher DeMarcus Lawrence swarmed as Maye began to backtrack from the pocket, and Maye saw Hollins — that same Hollins who had cashed in on fourth-and-9 minutes earlier — so he risked a prayer to the end zone.

With pressure in Maye's face, and an off-platform throw sapping some of his normal strength, the ball began its downward arc short of Hollins.

For the third time on Wednesday night, a Seahawks defender rather than a Patriots teammate proved in better position to make the catch.

Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe jumped the route and tapped each of his feet in the end zone as Hollins leapt behind him.

"It was something where we had a certain protection on it and were cutting and was trying to get rid of it and realized Mack was in the back there in the back and didn't put enough on it to get it out," Maye said after the Patriots' 13-10 loss. "It was just unacceptable. We had a chance to send it to overtime at the worst and the only thing you [can't] do is turn the ball over.

An erosion of the Patriots' second-half patience allowed Seattle to score 13 unanswered points after New England had built a slow but steady 10-0 lead. A drastic momentum swing in the third quarter carried the Seahawks from a team struggling to play complementary football after a hip injury limited quarterback Sam Darnold to one series … to a firing-on-all-cylinders team sandwiching a YAC-heavy touchdown between two takeaways.

Maye was hardly responsible for all of the swing: His stat line won't fully capture his receivers' drops, the pressure his offensive line began to allow, nor the 41 yards after the catch his defensive teammates ceded to Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba on the touchdown between Maye's initial two interception drives.

But Maye's job as quarterback isn't to blame the loss of A.J. Brown (ankle) nor the dip in his protection as the game progressed. Maye's job isn't to publicly question whether offseason acquisition Romeo Doubs executed assignments as his quarterback intended nor whether Hollins should have batted away that last pass to ensure that if Hollins didn't catch it, nobody did.

So Maye stood at the postgame podium after falling four points short of a road upset and blamed himself for the second-half unraveling.

"I thought we had the game under control," the Patriots' third-year quarterback said. "I thought we had a good plan to try to start chipping away and be patient and, yeah, lost patience and it cost us.

"[I] realize it's a long season. But at the same time, you can't have those and it's unacceptable."

Patriots teammates defended their quarterback.

"If you haven't made a mistake in a football game, you either haven't played enough games or you're playing a video game," Hollins said. "He's a hell of a player. He's going to make more plays."

Seahawks showed more patience than Patriots in their second-half comeback

The Patriots didn't arrive in Seattle only as oddsmaker underdogs coming to watch the Seahawks unveil the banner from a Super Bowl game that seven months ago New England lost.

They also arrived in Seattle trying to rebound from a Super Bowl loss better than the 45% of post-1999 Super Bowl losers who haven't even made the playoffs, much less returned to the Super Bowl, the next year.

New England arrived to the 2026 season with a tougher schedule than last year's slate, in which 14 of its 17 regular-season games came against teams who would not advance to the playoffs. This year, they'll play nine games against 2025 playoff teams.

Wednesday night offered a chance to move past a spring of off-field headlines and a plethora of questions about how legitimate the 2025 Patriots, who beat a QB2-led Denver Broncos team in the AFC championship, were. This was a chance to show what their June 1 acquisition of Brown meant for their receiver room; a chance to show how their offensive line health and lineup had stabilized since the Super Bowl.

In the first half, Maye led that charge. The strategic quick game and checkdowns weren't as fun or gaudy as the deep balls that helped Maye to MVP runner-up last season. But they were effective to neutralize a talented rushing unit like Seattle's.

So the Patriots redefined success as avoiding three-and-outs, hoping staying on the field longer would eventually create opportunity. Seattle's defense?

"We're like, 'OK, we got to stay patient,'" safety Julian Love said. "We can't chase plays because when they throw it to us, we just got to catch it. … It's tough to do when you feel like you're down 10-0, 'I'm going to go chase this play.' But us, we're like, 'All right. Let the game come to you.'"

Brown had proven a reliable safety net for Maye in the first half of the receiver's first game as a Patriots. On third-and-4 in the second quarter, he muscled for 5 yards near the right sideline. On third-and-2, he drew a 34-yard defensive pass interference call off a flea-flicker that set up the Patriots' first score one play later.

Brown would come back with a 14-yard slant on third-and-3 against Seahawks cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett as Maye faced pressure. But when, 90 seconds into the third quarter, an awkward tackle sent Brown to the blue medical tent and then the tunnel for X-rays, the collective comfort taking checkdowns and awaiting big plays dissipated.

A field goal and three-and-out were unideal but manageable. Then came the deep pass Maye intended for Doubs down the left sideline, that instead was tipped by the Seahawks' Rodney Thomas and intercepted by Pritchett, who said he read Maye's eyes.

"I tried to force one down the sideline to Romeo …" Maye said. "Just stopped being patient."

Patience became even more of a challenge when the Seahawks, quarterbacked by Drew Lock , turned the gifted possession into their first touchdown drive of the game.

After Doubs dropped a pass on second-and-14, Maye dropped back and fired up the middle of the field toward receiver Demario Douglas in traffic.

Love jumped the route for an interception, knocking Maye off his process while freeing his own quarterback to play conservatively even before Jobe brought the takeaway count to three.

"I know what kind of defense we have," Lock told Yahoo Sports. "I know what playmakers we have on our side of the ball. It's just, take care of it and don't give it to them in good field position and give them easy points. Make it a long game, see who's going to pull it out at the end and take care of the ball is my main thing.

"And then sure enough, the classic rule of whoever wins the turnover battle is going to win the game, ends up playing out."

Hollins: 'You either move past it or you go 0-17. I'd rather move past it'

Shortly after nine o'clock in Seattle, and midnight in New England, Maye exited the Patriots' visiting locker room rolling his black backpack atop his black Away rollerboard suitcase. A dinner buffet line for bus-bound players awaited. Maye bypassed it, dropping his bags near the end of the line and heading toward a metal railing.

As he hunched over it, grasping the railing with each of his hands, he held court with the family members who'd traveled to support him. Maye's wife, Ann Michael, and father, former UNC quarterback Mark, stood across the railing to his left. Maye's three older brothers — Luke, Cole and Beau — towered to his right. The quarterback brushed his hand through his hair at some points in the conversation, bowing his head at others.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel walked past, shaking the four visiting Maye men's hands, giving Ann Michael a brief hug and slapping his quarterback on the back.

Conversation was steady if not jovial as Maye processed his first three-interception game across 30 regular-season outings and four playoff games. Vrabel had stated both that "you can't throw three interceptions" and also that "Drake knows that."

There was a sense the Patriots know what they need to do next even if questions linger on how they will do it and how soon Brown will rejoin them.

So as the Patriots hovered between the end of Wednesday in Seattle and beginning of Thursday in New England, Maye hovered between the lingering disappointment and the next-play, next-game mentality.

The Patriots were still competitive in the loss, earning 19 first downs and 277 net yards to the Seahawks' 13 and 285, respectively. Maye had still amassed 225 yards from scrimmage, including 47 rushing on seven carries, even if his second-half passing amounted to 13-of-21 for 110 yards, no scores and three interceptions.

At least 16 more games await on the Patriots' schedule.

"You either move past it or you go 0-17," Hollins said. "I'd rather move past it."

Three more 2025 playoff teams loom next on the schedule in the Pittsburgh Steelers , Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills .

With Brown's return timeline in question, patience will continue to prove key.

"These guys are here for me," Maye said. "I think they've done a great job in supporting me and have had my back. I've got to earn their trust. I know I have their trust, but I got to keep on putting better football out there. I think it's Week 1 but at the same time, there's a full season ahead but you got to get this going early.

"We got to start off on the right foot. I know what we had last year, but we got a new season, a new team, and we need to build that."
